{"fetched_at":"2026-06-12","jd_text":"Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships
Location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role
As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic’s products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities
- Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
- Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic’s GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
- Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
- Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
- Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
- Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic’s products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have
- 7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
- 3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
- Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
- Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
- Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
- Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
- A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have
- 5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
- Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

Logistics
Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience.
Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience.
Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position.
Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, Anthropic expects all staff to be in one of its offices at least 25% of the time. Some roles may require more time in office.
Visa sponsorship: Anthropic says it sponsors visas but cannot successfully sponsor every role and candidate.

# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000-$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (partner GTM context) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic is expanding the practical enterprise surface around Claude: an end-user offering, a developer platform, and infrastructure for
agent-based applications. The opportunity is not only to demonstrate model capability, but to help organizations turn it into durable
workflows with clear controls, adoption plans, and measurable business relevance.

The core scaling question is how a fast-growing ecosystem can deliver a consistent customer experience. Cloud providers, consultancies,
and technology vendors bring distribution and domain knowledge, but each can introduce different implementation assumptions. A strong
technical partner motion reduces that variation through reusable patterns, clear escalation paths, and shared quality expectations.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is an AI safety and research company organized as a public benefit corporation. Its external identity joins frontier-model
development with an emphasis on trustworthy deployment. Commercially, it operates across enterprise product usage, platform consumption,
and ecosystem-assisted customer delivery.

This model creates an important boundary: Anthropic supplies the core product and platform, while external firms can contribute account
access, industry expertise, systems integration, and organizational change support. The quality of that boundary will shape whether
customers experience Claude as a coherent product platform or as a collection of unrelated implementations.

For an architecture leader, the relevant operating model is therefore neither pure product support nor traditional consulting. It is a
multiplier model: create assets, learning loops, and technical standards that allow many external teams to deliver high-quality outcomes
without requiring central involvement in every engagement.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic’s public materials point to two connected adoption paths. Claude Enterprise addresses organizational use of AI, while the
platform enables developers to embed Claude into applications and agent workflows. Both paths require more than access provisioning:
customers need practical guidance for configuration, rollout, use-case prioritization, and ongoing expansion.

Enterprise deployment guidance describes a progression from setup through launch, enablement, and broader adoption. That framing signals
that implementation quality includes people, process, and governance alongside system design. Partners that can handle only the initial
technical work may leave customer value unrealized.

A central operating pressure is balancing common standards with local relevance. Anthropic needs reusable methods that travel across
partners and geographies, while allowing industry-specific workflows to remain credible. The most valuable field insight is likely the
insight that can be generalized into platform improvements, deployment guidance, or enablement materials.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
Relevant functional stakeholders include:

- Research and safety teams that shape the company’s public trust posture and technical principles.

The role’s leverage will come from translating partner and customer signals into structured decisions. That means separating urgent,
account-specific requests from recurring needs that justify a reusable asset, product change, or broader operating policy.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic presents its platform as a place to build applications and agents using Claude models and managed agent infrastructure. The
resulting architecture conversation can span model interaction, application logic, workflow orchestration, operational monitoring, user
experience, and organizational controls.

Anthropic’s public positioning emphasizes safety, accuracy, security, and user trust. In enterprise architecture, those attributes need
to become observable design choices rather than abstract messages. Customers and partners will look for practical ways to address access
boundaries, evaluation approaches, workflow guardrails, human review, and operational ownership.

The most useful partner-ready assets would likely make sound practices easier to repeat. Examples include solution blueprints,
use-case qualification methods, implementation checklists, adoption playbooks, and structured mechanisms for identifying product gaps.
Such assets can improve speed while preserving the rigor expected of a company differentiated by responsible AI.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly describes a network of cloud, technology, and services partners focused on customer AI challenges. This indicates an
ecosystem designed as a meaningful route to adoption rather than a peripheral referral program.

The partner landscape has distinct sources of leverage:

- Technology vendors can connect Claude to established business systems, data environments, and application workflows.

Accenture’s public alliance messaging connects Anthropic’s models with enterprise deployment, productivity, and new-product development.
That is a useful signal: joint value propositions must bridge technical capability and the real operating environment in which customers
adopt it.

The central ecosystem challenge is not partner count. It is whether partners can independently recognize appropriate opportunities,
design credible solutions, manage risk thoughtfully, and deliver outcomes that reinforce Anthropic’s product reputation.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s current public surface includes Claude Enterprise, a developer platform, managed infrastructure for agents, enterprise
adoption resources, and a formal partner network. Taken together, these signals suggest a transition from access to models toward more
repeatable enterprise and application deployment.

That transition increases the importance of operating discipline. As the partner base grows, inconsistent solution designs or weak
feedback loops can create fragmented customer experiences and obscure the highest-priority product needs. Conversely, well-managed
implementation learning can compound into stronger product guidance, faster onboarding, and clearer market differentiation.

Enterprise buyers increasingly assess AI providers on the full path from evaluation to operational use. Anthropic’s safety-oriented
reputation can become a commercial advantage when customers see it reflected in practical deployment methods, not merely in research
claims or product messaging.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Ecosystem technical strategy across hyperscalers, consulting firms, and technology providers.
- Reusable enterprise AI solution patterns that reduce dependence on one-off demonstrations.
- Partner learning systems that improve independent execution and customer-facing quality.
- Industry workflow design connected to modern model and agent capabilities.
- Cross-functional technical leadership across commercial, product, engineering, and trust stakeholders.
- Adoption architecture that treats user readiness, governance, and operating ownership as design inputs.
- Field intelligence systems that convert recurring implementation signals into scalable assets.
- Responsible-AI practices that make trust, security, and reliability concrete for enterprise customers.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- A trust-centered company narrative creates room to discuss architecture governance as a market differentiator.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims, achievements, scope, metrics, and leadership evidence must come
from the governed resume and proof graph.
